Tip: A conducting sphere behaves like a point charge outside.

formulas.name: Coupled coils — dot convention
notes: Where: L₁ = self inductance, M = mutual inductance (H); + when both currents enter dotted ends
Tip: Both currents entering dotted ends → +M (aiding); one entering, one leaving → −M.

formulas.name: Series coupled coils
notes: Where: +2M aiding, −2M opposing
Tip: Measure aiding and opposing: M = (L<sub>aid</sub> − L<sub>opp</sub>)/4.

formulas.name: Coupling coefficient & energy
notes: Where: 0 ≤ k ≤ 1
Tip: Ideal transformer: k = 1.

formulas.name: Magnetic circuit with air gap
f: Total MMF = Σ H l = ϕ(S<sub>iron</sub> + S<sub>gap</sub>)
notes: Where: H = field strength (A/m), l = path length (m), φ = flux (Wb), S = reluctance (AT/Wb), l<sub>g</sub> = gap length, A = area (m²)
Tip: The tiny air gap usually needs most of the MMF because μ<sub>r</sub>(air) = 1.

formulas.name: Parallel magnetic paths
f: MMF across parallel paths is equal
notes: Where: φ = flux (Wb) in each path
Tip: Exactly like parallel resistors (Kirchhoff for flux).

formulas.name: Leakage & fringing
f: Leakage coefficient λ = total flux / useful flux ( > 1)
notes: Where: λ = leakage coefficient (1.1–1.25 typical)
Tip: Fringing increases the effective air-gap area.
